taxonomic_note: Accepted hybrid × formula and scientific concept verified against Kew; the iNaturalist observation omits the multiplication symbol in its taxon label. Distinguishing hybrid anatomy requires separate visual review.
look_here_first: SHORTSPIKE WINDMILLGRASS is the accepted seed-producing natural hybrid of Chloris cucullata × C. verticillata, documented in USDA NRCS Welder Germplasm accession 9085260 / PI 645601. The installed windmill photo is still a SOURCE-LABELLED candidate, not a voucher. Check longish 5–16 one-sided racemes, upper sterile oblong lemma ~1.7–2.2 mm and shorter ~1–2 mm awn versus fertile lemma ~2.2–2.9 mm with ~2–5 mm awn on the SAME specimen. Parent images don't prove hybrid identity. Macro-voucher hold stays.

authenticated_plant_reference.provenance: Welder Germplasm accession 9085260; PI 645601; selected class natural plant material (not evidence about a particular Hays plant).

kew_diagnostic.habit: Perennial, often stoloniferous, 30–70 cm tall, flattened keeled sheaths, ciliate membrane ligule about 2 mm.
kew_diagnostic.racemes: 5–16 digitate/unilateral racemes, each about 3–17.6 cm; whorls may vary, no sole-head hybrid proof.
kew_diagnostic.fertile_lemma: 2.2–2.9 mm long; short subapical awn about 2–5 mm.
kew_diagnostic.sterile_lemma: Upper barren lemma 1.7–2.2 mm, typically oblong NOT big rounded hood, its own awn 1–2 mm.
kew_diagnostic.field_protocol: Photograph same intact seedhead and 2 discrete lemmas and awns with 1 mm scale. Comparison to actual parents is educational, not individual hybrid verification.

historical_plate_reference_20261022.citation: A. S. Hitchcock and Agnes Chase, Manual of the Grasses of the United States, page 529, figure 768 (Chloris subdolichostachya; Heller 1679, Texas). Figure 770 on the same plate depicts C. cucullata.
historical_plate_reference_20261022.rights: Public domain historical botanical illustration as documented by Wikimedia Commons; link supplied as a research/teaching reference, NOT a downloaded photograph.
historical_plate_reference_20261022.content: The plate shows a radiating hybrid panicle and a separately drawn floret, paired with a distinct drawing of the hooded-windmillgrass parent. It helps explain exactly which reproductive unit to isolate for the next microscope session.
historical_plate_reference_20261022.caution: Printed ×5 floret drawing and another species' drawing are NOT an authenticated modern hybrid spikelet microphoto, a same-plant awn measurement, or a voucher for the existing iNaturalist candidate.

published_floristic_key_20261022.source: Flora of North Central Texas, Poaceae/Chloris key and species description, p. 1256
published_floristic_key_20261022.diagnostic: Upper sterile floret commonly squared off and nearly as wide as long, sometimes triangular; the upper margins of the lower (fertile) lemmas lack a prominent tuft of hairs. The lower fertile lemma is 2.2–2.9 mm long and not conspicuously one-sided swollen (not gibbous).
published_floristic_key_20261022.limits: Morphology overlaps C. cucullata and C. verticillata, and the historical key alone cannot establish a single photographed individual as the hybrid.

visual_comparison.overlay_note:
FIRST image is source-reported candidate only. Other two are separate parents C. cucullata and C. verticillata, not proof of hybrid. A mature stereo-microscope voucher with BOTH fertile and sterile awn lengths is essential.
Confirmation checklist (source: Kew POWO / GrassBase — Chloris × subdolichostachya): Separate lemma BODY length from AWN length. Fertile lemma: 2.2–2.9 mm; its awn: 2–5 mm. Examine the single upper sterile floret: oblong body 1.7–2.2 mm, with a 1–2 mm awn. Record the full combination on the same mature plant. Parent-like or intermediate head shape alone cannot establish hybrid identity. Still provisional: The existing windmill-head photograph cannot verify these microscopic traits or hybrid parentage.
